name: Horse Brass Pub
why: Fifty years and a real part in Oregon's craft beer history earn top story marks, and atmosphere rests on that pub culture rather than a room description we could source. The fish and chips are good pub food, not a destination of their own, and the place is famous.
story: Don Younger opened this English pub on Belmont in 1976 and poured cask ales, imports and some of Oregon's first microbrews. Willamette Week's oral history says the state's brewpub bill was plotted there. It marked 50 years in July 2026 by opening the Pony Room across the breezeway.
tagline: Cask ales and imports on Belmont since 1976
order: The halibut fish and chips, which Willamette Week counts among the best in town, with a cask ale.
practical: Shows Premier League matches (listed on the league's US bar finder)
The Pony Room, a companion space across the breezeway, opened in July 2026
hours: Mon-Fri 11 am-2:30 am, Sat-Sun 9 am-2:30 am (older Fearless Critic listing; unconfirmed)
flags: Hours unconfirmed: from an older Fearless Critic listing; another guide says 11:30 am-2 am daily. 'late' kept on that basis, please confirm. The pub's own site blocked my fetch.
Weekend 9 am opening and early openings for English football are unconfirmed, so 'morning' is left off.
Football detail rests only on the Premier League US bar finder listing.
Discovery lead's Scotch eggs and sausage rolls not confirmed by a citable source, left out.
Anniversary timing: the press release dates the founding to 1976 and the party to July 10-16, 2026; a Sunnyside neighborhood Q&A says the full 50th falls in November 2026.
Most recent dated coverage: Sunnyside neighborhood association Q&A, August 2026.

name: Pinolo Gelato
why: Faithful, much-praised gelato earns a strong signature mark, but it is a tidy shop on the ground floor of an apartment building with a short, simple story, so atmosphere and story stay modest.
story: Sandro Paolini, a Pisa native, opened this Tuscan-style gelateria on Division in 2015. The classics stay Italian, from Sicilian pistachio to organic Italian chocolate, while dairy-free sorbetti follow local fruit through the seasons. Portland Monthly calls it a contender for the city's best scoop of any kind.
tagline: Tuscan gelato from a Pisa native since 2015
order: Pistachio, made with Sicilian nuts, or whichever seasonal fruit sorbetto is in the case. An affogato if you want coffee too.
practical: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays (winter hours)
Espresso from Caffe Umbria, plus affogato
Dairy-free flavors change daily; the shop posts them on Instagram
hours: Winter: Wed, Thu, Sun noon-9 pm; Fri-Sat noon-10 pm; closed Mon-Tue (own site)
flags: Discovery lead said to order the pine nut flavor the shop is named for; the shop's current flavor list shows no pine nut flavor, so I left it out.
Lead's lidded steel wells (pozzetti) not confirmed by any source, left out.
Hours are the site's posted winter hours; summer hours may run later. Older listings showed a 10:30 pm close, but no current source shows past 10 pm, so no 'late'.
Own site's blog stops in 2021; most recent dated evidence it's open is Portland Monthly's Division/Clinton guide, Feb 27, 2026.
Early coverage gave the address as 3703 SE Division St; current sources use 3707.

name: Nuestra Cocina
why: A long-running, husband-and-wife Mexican room with one real detail in the hand-pressed tortillas. We found no recent press and no description of the room, so atmosphere and signature sit mid-range.
story: Chef Benjamin Gonzales and Shannon Dooley-Gonzales, husband and wife, have run this Division Street dining room since 2004, cooking rustic Mexican food with recipes from Zacatecas to the Veracruz coast. Every evening a tortilla maker presses corn tortillas by hand, on a press the chef's grandfather built.
tagline: Hand-pressed tortillas on a press grandpa built
order: Anything that comes with the corn tortillas, pressed by hand each evening and served hot. The kitchen counts them as a signature.
practical: The Mole Room hosts private group dinners
Chef Benjamin teaches private cooking classes on request
flags: Hours unconfirmed: the own site lists none; listing sites show Tue-Sat evenings and closed Mondays. 'when' is based on those listings.
Founding year 2004 is from Wikipedia; another guide says 2003.
Story and order rest mostly on the restaurant's own site.

Most recent evidence it's open is its appearance in a Portland Tribune health-inspection roundup, March 3, 2026; I did not see its score (the lead's 'perfect score' is unconfirmed). No recent press found.
Fame set to open-secret from Wikipedia coverage and older Portland press; I did not open a press review.
Lead's moles not confirmed as a dish on the current menu, left out.
Area: Wikipedia places it in Hosford-Abernethy; the candidate said Division-Clinton.

name: Original Hotcake House
why: A real 1963 institution with a hotcake people know by name, but the all-night hours that made it famous are gone and our sources say little about the room itself.
story: The Original Hotcake House has held the foot of the Ross Island Bridge since 1963, a counter-service greasy spoon that spent decades feeding Portland's after-bar crowd. It no longer stays open around the clock, but the feel survived, and the hotcakes still come with big scoops of butter sliding into the syrup.
order: The hotcakes, obviously. For a little of everything, get the combo of two eggs and two cakes.
practical: Counter service
No longer open 24 hours
flags: Status unclear: the newest dated independent source is The Infatuation, Sep 10, 2025, just outside the 12-month window. Confirm before approving.

Open status: the newest dated independent source is The Infatuation's review of Sep 10, 2025, about a month outside the 12-month window. Discovery's Dec 2025 sighting was directory reviews, which don't count. Please confirm it's open before publishing.

Hours unconfirmed: no current published schedule found. Willamette Week (Jan 2023) said it closed at 11 pm, and The Infatuation (Sep 2025) says it is no longer 24 hours. Dropped 'late' for lack of a current source; 'evening' rests on the 2023 report.
Discovery's jukebox and 'flipping until 11 pm' details came from a May 2024 Willamette Week piece I didn't open, so they are left out.

name: Off The Griddle
why: A likable cart-to-cafe story and a fun Taco Bell riff on the menu, but vegan brunch is well covered in Portland and nothing we found makes the room memorable.
story: Off The Griddle began in 2010 as a food cart at SE 50th and Division, one hauled in from a field near Boise. A cafe on Burnside came next, then this restored corner at 65th and Foster in 2017. Brunch is vegan by default, with a full bar and a Bloody Mary list.
tagline: Vegan brunch that began as a 2010 food cart
order: The brunch wrap supreme, their Taco Bell riff with soy chorizo, tofu scramble and house cheese sauce. Real scrambled eggs can be swapped in for $2 more.
practical: Vegan by default, eggs on request for $2
Full bar with brunch cocktails
Second location at 2215 NE Alberta St
flags: History (2010 cart at 50th and Division, Burnside cafe, Boise cart) is from the owner's site only.
Open evidence: Portland Monthly's brunch guide (Nov 2025 per discovery; I couldn't see a date on the page) plus own-site blog posts from 2026. No independent source dated 2026 found.
Not fully vegan as discovery said: Portland Monthly says eggs can be swapped in, and the own site calls it a vegan restaurant that is vegetarian-friendly.
Two locations (Foster and NE Alberta), so not a chain by our rule. This draft is the Foster original.

name: Master Kong
why: Tianjin cooking is rare here and the congee with fried dough is a true signature. The house setting is homey rather than striking, and the story is short since it opened in 2018.
story: Master Kong opened in March 2018 in a small house on Division, where siblings cook a mix of northern Tianjin and southern Cantonese home food. Breakfast congee with a hot fried dough stick for dunking is the draw. Willamette Week named it newcomer of the year in 2018, and a Richmond location followed in 2022.
tagline: Sibling-run congee house on Division since 2018
order: A bowl of congee (black chicken, clam, or preserved egg and pork) with the fried dough stick on the side for dunking. The Tianjin-style steamed buns, goubuli baozi, are the regional specialty.
practical: About 35 seats in a converted house
Second location on SE 32nd Ave in Richmond
hours: Daily 9 am-9 pm (Portland Monthly listing, undated)
flags: Hours unconfirmed: Portland Monthly's undated listing says daily 9 am-9 pm, but Willamette Week in 2018 had it closed Mondays. Check before publishing.
Sibling ownership and the goubuli baozi detail come from 2018 Willamette Week and Portland Monthly search snippets; current ownership not rechecked.
Open evidence: Portland Tribune inspection list (Jun 4, 2026) at 8435 SE Division, and a finalist for Best Chinese in Willamette Week's 2026 readers' poll (Jul 2026).
Area: Wikipedia and Portland Monthly place it in Montavilla; discovery said Jade District. Two locations, so not a chain.

name: Mis Tacones
why: A queer- and Chicano-owned vegan taqueria with a real pop-up history and national recognition scores well on story. We found little about the room and no hours, which holds atmosphere back.
story: Mis Tacones is a Chicano- and queer-owned vegan taqueria that started in 2016 as a pop-up, cooking seitan tacos at markets and queer dance nights. The Killingsworth restaurant opened in 2022 and has offered free meals to trans people of color. In 2026 the New York Times named it among the country's best Mexican restaurants.
tagline: Vegan pop-up turned New York Times pick
order: Tacos on tortillas pressed to order, filled with house-made seitan al pastor or asada and finished with chipotle crema.
practical: Fully vegan menu
Free meals for trans people of color, per a 2022 report
flags: Hours unconfirmed: no hours source found. 'midday' rests on Eater Portland's 2025 lunch lists (cited on Wikipedia); evening service is likely but unsourced.

The New York Times listing (41 best Mexican restaurants, Aug 13, 2026) is confirmed through Wikipedia's citations, which also cite KOIN and the Portland Tribune (Aug 18, 2026); I didn't open the Times piece itself.
Discovery's lead left out that it is fully vegan, a key fact for readers.
Free-meals policy and order details come from 2021-2022 Oregonian and Eater reporting quoted on Wikipedia; worth checking they still hold.
Open evidence: finalist for Best Mexican and Best Vegan in Willamette Week's 2026 readers' poll (Jul 2026) and the NYT list (Aug 2026).

name: John Street Cafe
why: A well-liked St. Johns breakfast cafe with a real signature in the filbert-and-currant pancakes, but the format is common and the story is thin: no founding year or owner names, only an undated note that it changed hands.
story: A breakfast-and-lunch cafe on the St. Johns stretch of Lombard that Willamette Week was already recommending in 2011. Omelets anchor the menu, the filbert-and-currant pancakes come huge, and there's a sunny patio. It changed hands at some point, and one restaurant guide says the new owners kept things as they were.
tagline: Filbert-and-currant pancakes and a sunny patio
order: The giant filbert-and-currant pancakes. If you want savory, the omelets are what the kitchen is built around.
practical: Breakfast and lunch only
Patio seating
Kid-friendly
hours: Wed-Sun, breakfast and lunch from 7 am (Willamette Week 2013 listing and Portland Monthly listing); current hours unconfirmed
flags: Status unclear: no dated evidence it is open since Nov 2025. Confirm before approving.

Open status unconfirmed: no citable source dated after Nov 2025. The only recent sign of life is discovery's Jun 2026 OpenStreetMap re-survey, which couldn't be checked this run. Please confirm it's open before approving.
Hours come from a 2013 Willamette Week listing and a partial, undated Portland Monthly listing; current days and closing time unconfirmed.
Portland Monthly's page blocked our fetch; the pancake, omelet and patio details come from its search-result text (listing undated).
Ownership change is from an undated Gayot review; owners unnamed, and no founding year found anywhere.
Portland Mercury has a john-street-cafe tag page (not opened); counted toward fame along with Willamette Week and Portland Monthly.

name: B&b Pizza Co.
why: A modest draft: a two-year-old family pizza parlor whose old-school concept, salad bar and sourdough-cornmeal crust set it apart from chain pizza, and local readers voted it best pizza in 2026. The story is short, the room is a big family space with TVs, and only one outlet has covered it.
story: Co-owner Jason Blume spent nearly 20 years behind the bar and in the owner's seat at Skyland Pub before opening B&b in fall 2024. He wanted the feel of the family pizza parlors he grew up with, salad bar included. The thin crust is house sourdough with cornmeal, and the sauce is made in-house.
tagline: Sourdough pies and a salad bar, parlor style
order: A thin sourdough-crust pie and a trip to the salad bar. For a quick lunch, slices come with up to three toppings of your choice.
practical: Salad bar
Pizza by the slice
Full bar plus a soda fountain
Big tables for groups
hours: Sun-Thu 11 am-9 pm, Fri-Sat 11 am-10 pm (The Outlook, Mar 2026)
flags: Single source: The Outlook (Pamplin) Readers' Choice feature, March 2026. The own site (bandbpizza.co) was not opened, and no other press turned up.
Opened fall 2024, so about two years in place. Reviewer should judge whether it is too new, and too much a roomy family restaurant with sports on TV, for a hole-in-the-wall guide.
Directory listings show a Godfather's Pizza at the same address, probably the previous tenant. Not confirmed, and not used.
Hours come from the March 2026 article, not the own site. Closes at 10 pm at the latest, so no late tag.
Best Pizza is a readers' vote in a local paper, not a critic's pick.

name: Kelly's Olympian
why: The room and its 124 years carry the marks: motorcycles overhead, original neon, a stage busy most nights. Signature is low because the food is ordinary bar fare, and a refresh that wrapped up this week, with offices moving in upstairs, could soften the feel.
story: Kelly's has poured on this downtown corner since 1902 and calls itself Portland's oldest dive bar. Motorcycles hang over the drinkers, the neon sign is the original, and the stage has music most nights. It reopened Oct. 27, 2026, after a refresh, as coworking offices moved in upstairs.
order: A drink under the motorcycles and whoever is on stage that night. Happy hour runs 5 to 7 pm every day, and the kitchen serves burger baskets and other bar food late.
practical: Live music most nights, some shows ticketed
Kitchen open late every night
Happy hour daily 5 to 7 pm
20% gratuity added for parties of 5 or more
hours: Mon 5 pm-1 am, Tue-Wed 1 pm-1 am, Thu-Sun 1 pm-2 am (own site, Oct 2026)
flags: Just reopened on Oct. 27, 2026 after a refresh, per its own site, with UrbanWork coworking taking the five floors above. How long it was closed and what changed in the bar is unconfirmed. A Hoodline piece (AI-rewritten news, not cited) put the work at about $750,000; check real press before publishing.
Origin conflict kept out of the story: the own site says it began as a card room and cigar shop, while Wikipedia (search snippet) says it opened as the Olympian Saloon tied to Olympia Brewing.
The oldest-dive-bar and third-oldest-bar titles are the bar's own claims, and the recent closure sits awkwardly with continuously operating.
Hours, menu and the live-music claim come from the own site only, posted for the reopening.
Wikipedia and the Willamette Week pieces were seen in search results, not opened. The motorcycles are confirmed by both the own site and a WW headline.

name: Ken's Artisan Bakery
why: Story and signature lead: a pioneering levain bakery now owned by two longtime employees, with loaves and a croissant that have lasted more than two decades. It is famous and on every list, so uniqueness sits around 60 among Portland's many good bakeries, and we found nothing that describes the room.
story: Ken Forkish opened this bakery on NW 21st in 2001 and built its name on long-fermented levain loaves. He sold it at the end of 2021 to two longtime employees, on staff since 2002 and 2005, and retired. They have since added an annex a few doors away.
tagline: Forkish's 2001 bakery, now owned by its staff
order: An Oregon Croissant, a fixture almost since the bakery opened, and a Country Bread #2 to take home.
practical: Lunch served from 10 am
Annex at 320 NW 21st Ave, open Thursday to Monday
hours: Daily 8 am-4 pm, lunch from 10 am; annex Thu-Mon 7 am-2 pm (own site, seen in search results)
flags: The own site returned no readable text to our fetch, so hours, the annex and menu names (Country Bread #2) come from search-result snippets of kensartisan.com. Time Out lists different, probably older hours (Mon-Sat 7 am-6 pm, Sun 8 am-5 pm). Confirm.

Founding year, the end-of-2021 sale and the staff start years (2002 and 2005) come from search snippets of Wikipedia, Willamette Week (Jan 2022) and Portland Food and Drink. Those pages were not opened.

Most recent dated coverage: Willamette Week's Oregon Croissant piece, Feb 2026, seen in search results only. What goes into the Oregon Croissant was not confirmed, so the order names it without describing it.
Not a chain: the bakery plus its annex on the same block. Ken's Artisan Pizza was sold separately in the same 2021-22 sale and is a different business now.
The lead's claim that it taught Portland slow-fermented bread was left out as unsourced.
Very well known. It fits as a local legend, not a discovery.

name: Nicholas Restaurant
why: A strong family story since 1987 and a 2026 readers' poll win carry it. The 2021 move to a larger, more polished building costs it atmosphere, and we could not source a specific dish, which holds down signature.
story: Nicholas Dibe arrived from Lebanon, then at war, and opened this family restaurant on SE Grand in 1987. After 33 years there, the family moved it to a roomier building on SE Madison in 2021 and turned the old space into a fast-casual spinoff, Beirut Bites.
order: Go with friends and share a spread of Lebanese plates at the place Willamette Week readers voted Portland's best Mediterranean restaurant in 2026.
practical: Second location in Gresham, 323 N Main Ave
Moved from SE Grand in 2021; the old space is now Beirut Bites
flags: Address changed: the candidate's 318 SE Grand Ave is the original location, which the family turned into Beirut Bites (WW, July 2022). Nicholas moved to 1109 SE Madison St in 2021 (own site, WW).

Location count: the own site lists two (SE Madison, and Gresham at 323 N Main Ave). Wikipedia (search snippet) calls it a chain of three, probably counting a NE Broadway branch that listings suggest may have closed. Beirut Bites trades under a different name. Under 4 by our rule either way, but check Broadway.

No dish sourced: the giant house pita and mezza platters in the lead appear only in review-site and ordering-page snippets, which we can't cite. The Infatuation or WW 2018 review probably covers them; add one before publishing.
Hours unconfirmed: our fetch of the own site showed no hours. The when tags are kept from the candidate record.
Open evidence: won Best Mediterranean Restaurant in the Willamette Week readers' poll, July 2026.
Wikipedia and the WW move and spinoff pieces were seen in search results, not opened.
Address corrected to 1109 SE Madison St (discovery had 318 SE Grand Ave); coordinates from an OpenStreetMap address search.

name: Jam on Hawthorne
why: A well-liked, busy brunch cafe with one real quirk, the jam made on site, and good vegan plates. Uniqueness and story are modest: it is a solid version of a common thing, and we found little history beyond the owners and a 2011 expansion.
story: Jam on Hawthorne takes its name from the jams it cooks in house, and it serves breakfast every day in a big, busy room. It grew into a former bar space next door in 2011. Vegans eat well here, with tofu scramble and tempeh bacon, and readers keep ranking it among Portland's top brunches.
tagline: Named for the jam it cooks in house
order: The two-egg breakfast with a mimosa, the pairing Willamette Week once called the move here, or the tofu scramble with tempeh bacon if you're vegan. Expect a wait.
practical: Expect a wait at brunch
Vegan and gluten-free options
Breakfast served every day
flags: Hours unconfirmed: no own site turned up, only directory listings (roughly 8 am-2 pm). Wikipedia says breakfast is served daily. The when tags rest on that.

No sister restaurants under the Jam name found. The owners, Gordon Feighner and Katie Prevost, also run Cricket Cafe on SE Belmont (Wikipedia, citing 2017 Eater and WW coverage); its current status was not checked.
Most facts come through Wikipedia's summaries of Eater, Oregonian, Mercury and WW pieces from 2011 to 2021; the underlying articles were not opened. Founding year not found.
Open evidence: second place, Best Brunch Spot, Willamette Week readers' poll, July 2026.
Wikipedia mentions a kids' play area in the past tense; left out.
A famous brunch line rather than a discovery; the readers' polls measure popularity, not character.
